facts.population: Patients in RCTs of implant placement (two included RCTs: 59 fully edentulous patients; 51 fully or partially edentulous patients)
facts.intervention: Computer-guided (digital workflow) implant placement with 3D planning and surgical guide
facts.main_result: Only two RCTs qualified; no statistically significant differences in implant survival or patient outcomes between guided and conventional placement, though one RCT reported more pain and swelling in the conventional group.
facts.sample_size: 2 RCTs included (59 and 51 patients) from 37 screened abstracts
facts.follow_up: 1 year in both included RCTs (minimum 6 months required)
facts.limitations: Based on only two RCTs with risk of bias; overall scientific evidence is low.
facts.key_finding: This critical review of RCTs found only two eligible trials comparing computer-guided with conventional implant placement. Implant survival and patient outcomes did not differ significantly, with less pain and swelling reported in the guided group of one trial.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Guided surgery performs similarly to free-hand placement in survival; it may be justified for flapless surgery, optimal positioning and immediate loading, but firm recommendations cannot be given.
